trade.structure: Outright short MX CRAH27 / CORRA_2027-03 in implied-rate space (pay CORRA, short duration). Canonical side short profits if the packet implied-rate mark rises from 3.13. Paper at the frozen tradable-curve mid only.
trade.thesis: FACT: CORRA overnight is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17; the 3m strip prices 2.775 by Dec-26, 3.13 by Mar-27 (+84.0bp vs overnight), 3.365 by Jun-27 and a 2028 peak near 3.655. US SOFR jumped to 3.85 after the Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; SR3H7 is 4.565 and SR3U7 peaks at 4.735. Canada Q2 GDP was +0.8% q/q after +0.1% in Q1, Ivey PMI accelerated, household consumption +0.8% q/q and disposable income +2.1% q/q. Headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%. BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; the last-24 desk thesis says the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse after the Fed hike, BoJ 25bp to 1.25%, and a BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes. INFERENCE: 2.29 is an over-insurance setting against the August jobs print, not an equilibrium compatible with still-positive activity and a global tightening regime. Mar-27 at 3.13 still prices a shallow catch-up versus US 4.565 and versus Canada's own 2028 CRA peak near 3.65, so paying Mar-27 owns the residual hike impulse without needing a new 10Y term-premium story. UNKNOWN: whether energy pass-through actually shows up in subsequent CPI, and whether August employment -42k is the start of a demand break.
trade.mispricing: FACT: CA-US 2Y is -140bp (1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.31, 1m change -17bp) and CA 2Y is 3.27 versus US 2Y 4.76. CORRA_2027-03 at 3.13 versus SOFR_2027-03 at 4.565 is a 143.5bp policy-path gap. INFERENCE: the market still prices a deep relative Canada slowdown and a BoC that only partially converges. That assumption is too pessimistic relative to Canada activity 66, Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q, and a global hike impulse that has already been delivered in the US and Japan. The edge is not 'percentiles must mean-revert'; it is that overnight 2.29 plus a 3.13 Mar-27 contract understates the catch-up required if activity and energy pass-through dominate labor.
why_now: FACT: the Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% is delivered and SOFR printed 3.85 on 2026-09-17; last-24 adds BoJ 1.25% and a BoE 6-3 split with three hike votes, so the tightening impulse is no longer a US-only story.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether Canada’s still-positive activity and a global energy-constrained tightening regime force the BoC off a 2.29 CORRA setting. Mechanism: resilient North American growth plus energy pass-through keep Canadian inflation from settling at core-near-2%, so the policy path has to catch US/AONIA rather than stay on labor-insurance hold. The Mar-27 CORRA contract is where that catch-up is still incomplete.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: overnight CORRA 2.29; 1m strip 2.2875 in Sep-26 then 2.58 by Dec-26; 3m strip 2.385/2.775/3.13/3.365/3.51 into Sep-27 and a 2028 peak of 3.655. CA 2Y 3.27 is +31bp over 1m but -8bp on 1d; CA 10Y 3.83. US 2Y 4.76 is +57bp over 1m after the Sep-16 Fed hike (futures had >90% odds of 25bp) and SOFR’s 3.62 to 3.85 jump on 2026-09-17. USDCAD 1.4010 is a 74th 1y / 87th 5y percentile after +1.74% over 1m. INFERENCE: Canada front-end has started repricing, but the overnight setting and Mar-27 3.13 still lag the delivered US hike and the global-tightening cluster.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: Canada headline CPI 3% with core/trim/median near 2%; August employment -42k; CA activity gauges already showed Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q; Fed hike was >90% priced into Sep-16. NEW in this packet’s last-24/desk cluster: BoJ +25bp to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 with three hike votes, and the desk thesis that energy is shutting the global easing impulse. ALSO NEW relative to a fully priced Fed hike: official SOFR 3.85 versus the pre-hike 3.62 print. The Saudi Oman STS workaround is new as a tail-risk reducer, not as proof that energy inflation is gone.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: FACT: CORRA_2027-03 at 3.13 implies about +84bp of tightening from 2.29 by early 2027 and a terminal near 3.65, still ~90bp below the US SR3 peak of 4.735 and ~129bp below AONIA’s 2027 mid-4.9s. Combined with CA-US 2Y at -140bp, the market requires a materially softer Canadian cycle than the US and a BoC that only partially converges.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: INFERENCE: the priced Canada slowdown/on-hold residual is wrong. Activity and income/consumption still expanded in Q2, US gauges remain hot (activity 69, labor 75, inflation 72, consumer 74), and global policy is tightening, not easing. Labor 38 is real but is already in the 2.29 setting; it is not a reason for Mar-27 to cap at 3.13 if energy pass-through and activity hold.
context_build.price_decomposition: FACT: Canada 2s10s is 56bp, 0.60th percentile of 1y after -18bp over 1m — the 1m CA 2Y +31bp did most of the flattening. The STIR path still has a steep 2.29 to 3.13 to 3.65 climb, so the remaining discrepancy is the overnight/policy gap versus peers, not a 10Y term-premium story. US 2s10s 25bp is the 0.20th 1y percentile after a 2Y-led selloff. Marginal driver for this trade is the CORRA implied-rate strip, not USDCAD (which already cheapened CAD) and not CA 10Y (97th 5y percentile).

historical_reference.distribution: FACT: CA-US 2Y -140bp sits at 3.77th 1y / 4.31st 5y percentile (z 1y -1.84, z 5y -1.51); CA-US 5Y is 0.20th 1y. CA 2Y 3.27 is 97.8th 1y but only 58.5th 5y, so the 1y stretch is a recent catch-up from very low policy, not a 5y extreme. CA 2s10s 56bp is 0.60th 1y / 65.6th 5y. US 2Y 4.76 is 99.8th 1y / 88.0th 5y and US 10Y 5.01 is 99.6th 1y / 99.9th 5y. Those percentiles are discovery flags that Canada remains the laggard and that paying US duration is already the crowded extreme.

1994-style global tightening into still-positive activity, where front-end rates repriced higher as policy lagged growth. Packet does not provide a 1994 yield path; analog is qualitative only.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end Canada is a policy-path trade. The observable CORRA strip, not the CA 2Y 97th-percentile 1y print, is the priced BoC path. US SOFR/SR3 is the peer that Canada is supposed to converge toward. A sovereign 2Y percentile is not a substitute for that strip.

stir_policy_path.rationale: FACT: MX CRAH27 implied 3.13 versus overnight 2.29 is the residual BoC catch-up after a delivered Fed hike and a still-positive Canada activity impulse. US SOFR_2027-03 at 4.565 is a valid pay-growth STIR but US 2Y/10Y are already 99th-percentile 1y and SR3 already prices +88.5bp to the 4.735 peak, so the unused policy gap is in Canada not the US. AONIA is hiking from 4.35 with the housing channel already biting, so it is the wrong cyclical expression.

two_year.rationale: FACT: CA 2Y 3.27 is 97.8th 1y but only 58.5th 5y, +31bp over 1m and already -8bp on 1d. It echoes the same catch-up but mixes term premium with the policy path. The live BoC assumption lives in CORRA, and a 2Y percentile is not a substitute for the strip.

five_year.rationale: FACT: CA 5Y 3.54 is 97.8th 1y / 81.8th 5y, closer to the 2028 CRA peak of 3.65 than to overnight 2.29. Paying 5Y owns less of the near-term hike impulse and more duration than the discrepancy requires.

ten_year.rationale: FACT: CA 10Y 3.83 is 97.4th 1y / 96.8th 5y; US 10Y 5.01 is 99.9th 5y. Long-end already embeds term premium and the 1m move (+13bp CA, +36bp US) is smaller than the 2Y. This is not where the underpriced catch-up lives.

curve.rationale: FACT: CA 2s10s 56bp is 0.60th percentile of 1y after -18bp over 1m because 2Y already rallied. A growth-resilient hike catch-up is an outright pay-front-end view; a steepener would be the opposite (easing) expression, and a flattener mostly repeats a move that has already printed.

cross_market_rv.rationale: FACT: CA-US 2Y -140bp is 3.77th 1y / 4.31st 5y percentile and CORRA_2027-03 versus SOFR_2027-03 is 143.5bp. That is the cleanest relative statement that Canada is the laggard. It is not selected because receiving US 2Y/SOFR fights the same pro-growth global-hike regime (US gauges 69-75, Fed already hiking, SR3 still rising).

rates_tenor_scan.selection_rationale: CORRA_2027-03 is the best rates expression after scanning STIR, 2Y, 5Y, 10Y, curve, and CA-US RV: it is the markable MX CRA contract that still prices only +84bp of catch-up from 2.29, matching this seat's already-open book family, without receiving US duration.

expression_comparison.rationale: USDCAD 1.4010 already cheapened CAD (74th 1y / 87th 5y, +1.74% over 1m), so spot has partially expressed Canada lag plus the Fed hike. The remaining discrepancy is the 2.29 overnight / 3.13 Mar-27 CORRA path versus US 4.565. Rates are at least as clean as spot and are preferred. Long NZDUSD is a genuine risk-on alternative (5y percentile 8.61, Q2 GDP 0.2% q/q beat, India trade deal) but NZ policy/yields are unavailable, NZ labor 32 / consumer 38, and the desk thesis says energy keeps term-rate pressure elevated even where growth is softer — so NZD is not a cleaner owner of this packet's growth-versus-policy gap.
